title: Orderly Queue
description: You are given a lowercase string `s` and an integer `k`. In one move, you may pick any one of the first `k` characters of `s` and append it to the end of `s`. Return the lexicographically smallest string achievable after applying any number of moves.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.
hints: When k == 1, you can only rotate the string cyclically, so return the lexicographically smallest rotation.
When k >= 2, you can swap any two adjacent characters (bubble sort), which means any permutation is reachable—simply sort s.

examples.explanation: With k = 1, the rotations of "cba" are "cba", "bac", and "acb"; "acb" is smallest.
With k = 3 (>= 2), any permutation is reachable, so sorting gives "aaabc".

timeComplexity: O(n^2) for k=1, O(n log n) for k>=2
